_comment: Request flows for the step-through player. Each step names the diagram nodes and edges it lights up, and the file (and function, checked to exist in that file) where it happens.

flows.title: Opening a page
flows.summary: A page address becomes a file by way of site/site.json. Nothing else on disk can be reached.

steps.title: The browser asks for an address
steps.text: Typing /materials, following a link, or an old address such as /market_place_1.html.

steps.title: The guards run first
steps.text: The Host header must be this machine (or in ALLOWED_HOSTS), otherwise the answer is 421 before anything else happens. Every response then gets nosniff and no-referrer.

steps.title: site.json turns the address into a page
steps.text: The route table is built once from site/site.json: page routes, aliases (301 to the canonical route), design-time names (302). An address that is not in it is a 404; the file system is never searched.

steps.title: The built page is sent
steps.text: pages/<page>.html with Cache-Control: no-cache and conditional-request support, plus the page's own headers from site.json (the Design Studio gets cross-origin isolation for its in-browser models).

steps.title: Photos and videos come from /media
steps.text: The page asks for /media/m02-terracotta.jpg. Only allowed extensions are served, dot-segments and traversal are refused, and Range requests work so video seeks.

flows.title: Scanning a photo in the Design Studio
flows.summary: Browser to Express to Python and back: Gemini outlines the surfaces, SAM and edge snapping make the edges exact.

steps.title: The Studio posts the photo
steps.text: The Studio's server-mode code first asked /api/config what the server can do. Now it sends POST /api/segment with the photo as base64 and the chosen options (SAM on or off, edge refinement, model, a hint).

steps.title: Express guards the request
steps.text: Host check, then for a write under /api/: Content-Type must be application/json (415 before the body is read) and a present Origin must equal the Host (403).

steps.title: Is Google configured?
steps.text: If not, the answer is 503 FAILED_PRECONDITION with the reason, and Python is not called. The Studio shows the message and uses its in-browser parser.

steps.title: The body is streamed to Python
steps.text: No JSON parsing, no re-encoding of an 80 MB photo: the request is piped to POST /segment on 127.0.0.1 with the shared key in X-Terucon-Model-Key, and the answer is piped back. Five seconds to connect; after that Google may take minutes, so the silence limit is ten.

steps.title: Python checks and decodes
steps.text: Its own guards (Host, key, JSON only), then the image is decoded, rotated by its EXIF orientation and limited to 4096 px on the long side.

steps.title: Gemini names and outlines the surfaces
steps.text: detect.py asks Gemini (Vertex AI or an API key, through the service's own Google client) for every surface as a rough polygon with a kind: wall, floor, ceiling, window, door, furniture. If the configured model is not available to the project, the next one is tried.

steps.title: SAM corrects the outlines (if it is on)
steps.text: sam_refine corrects each outline, but only within a band around the outline's own edge, so SAM can fix a boundary and cannot wander off. Skipped when SAM is off or still loading.

steps.title: Every boundary snaps onto a real edge
steps.text: Contour snapping slides each boundary, outer edges and holes, along its normal onto the photo's edge, paying for every pixel it moves, so a good outline barely changes and a bad one is pulled in. It has an 8 second budget; surfaces it does not reach keep their outline.

steps.title: Layering and clean-up
steps.text: Structure goes below, windows and doors above, furniture on top. Specks and holes are cleaned, surfaces that end up too small are dropped, the rest are numbered 1..N and compressed into one label map.

steps.title: The answer goes back
steps.text: labelMap, metas (label, kind, share, source), scene, engine, model, notes, hints and timings stream through Express to the Studio, which paints the surfaces and names the engine in its footer.

flows.title: Scanning when the model service is down
flows.summary: The website works without Python. The Studio says why and uses its own parser.

steps.title: The Studio asks as usual
steps.text: POST /api/segment, exactly the same request.

steps.title: Express cannot reach Python
steps.text: The service may be starting, not installed (no Python with the packages), switched off with MODEL_SERVICE=off, or crashed and waiting for its next restart. Express knows which, because the supervisor tracks it and a cached health check confirms it.

steps.title: 503 UNAVAILABLE with a plain reason
steps.text: The message says what is wrong and what to do: still starting (try again in a moment), switched off (MODEL_SERVICE=off), Python or its packages missing (npm run setup:model), or the reason it crashed. The Studio shows it verbatim.

steps.title: The in-browser parser takes over
steps.text: SegFormer in a Web Worker names the surfaces from the photo on the person's own computer. Coarser edges, no Google and no server needed. The footer says which engine produced the surfaces.

steps.title: /api/config tells the truth meanwhile
steps.text: GET /api/config never fails because Python did: it reports model.status (starting, ready, unavailable, off) and a SAM state of unavailable or off, so the Studio's settings show the real situation.

flows.title: Rendering a finish
flows.summary: The credentials never leave the server: the browser sends a request, Express adds the sign-in.

steps.title: The Studio asks for a render
steps.text: POST /api/vertex/generate with {model, location?, body}: the body is what Gemini or Nano Banana would receive, including the photo and the chosen material.

steps.title: Guards and validation
steps.text: JSON only and same-origin as before, then the body must be {model, location?, body} (400 otherwise). The model name must match [A-Za-z0-9._-]{3,80} and the location [a-z0-9-]{2,40}; lib/vertex.js refuses anything else before any network call.

steps.title: Express signs in to Google
steps.text: A service-account key is exchanged for an access token (RS256-signed request to Google's token endpoint) and cached; application default credentials or an API key work too. The key is read from .env or the environment and never sent to the browser.

steps.title: generateContent, with patience
steps.text: The call goes to Vertex AI or the Gemini API. 429 and 5xx are retried up to 4 attempts honouring Retry-After, with exponential back-off; a 401 refreshes the token once; silence for 240 s after connecting is a 504 and is not retried; the whole call is capped at 330 s.

steps.title: Google's answer passes through
steps.text: Status and body come back unchanged (the Studio's model fallback is built on Google's own 404 messages), with X-Terucon-Attempts telling how many tries it took. One log line per call: model, status, seconds. No images, no keys.

flows.title: The SAM Pick tool
flows.summary: Click on a surface, get an exact mask. Needs SAM; until it has loaded the Studio uses SlimSAM in the browser.

steps.title: A click, or a box, on the photo
steps.text: The Studio sends POST /api/sam/refine with the points (and labels, or a box) and either the image_id it got earlier or the photo itself.

steps.title: The SAM key, if one is set
steps.text: When SAM_SERVER_KEY is set (a GPU box that other servers call) the request needs it as x-api-key or a Bearer token, compared in constant time. Otherwise 401.

steps.title: Streamed to the model service
steps.text: Same path as a scan: piped to POST /sam/refine. If the service is not usable, health answers 200 with status unavailable and the POSTs answer 503, so the Studio can say why.

steps.title: Is SAM ready?
steps.text: Off: 503 with the instruction to set SAM_ENABLED=true. Still loading: 503 UNAVAILABLE, try again in a moment (the Studio meanwhile uses SlimSAM in the browser). Error: the reason.

steps.title: The photo is embedded once
steps.text: The image embedding is cached per photo (by image_id), so the first click costs seconds and the next ones about a tenth of a second.

steps.title: The best mask comes back
steps.text: The backend predicts candidate masks, the highest score wins, and it is returned as a base64 PNG with the score, the image_id and the model label.

flows.title: Rebuilding the pages from a new Claude Design export
flows.summary: pages_original/ plus JSON patches become pages/. A changed export fails loudly instead of being half-patched.

steps.title: Drop the new export in place
steps.text: Replace the file in pages_original/ under the same name (index.html, market_place.html, Swatchroom.html, dashboard.html). These are never edited and never served.

steps.title: site.json says what is what
steps.text: Each page lists its source export and its built file; linkStyle decides whether links in the pages point at routes (/materials) or file names.

steps.title: npm run build:site
steps.text: The build reads site.json, decodes each export's bundle (template plus compressed assets) and applies the page's patch file.

steps.title: Anchored JSON patches
steps.text: site/patches/<page>.json is a list of steps: relink design-time names, insert the navigation entries from components.json, apply the Studio's server-mode snippets. Every anchor must match exactly the expected number of times, otherwise the build stops and says which step.

steps.title: pages/ is written
steps.text: The four built pages are written and committed. An untouched bundle round-trips byte for byte, so only the patched parts differ from the export.

steps.title: The links are checked
steps.text: npm run check:links verifies that every same-site link resolves, that every page links to the pages site.json requires, and that no design-time name is left. npm run check:site rebuilds in memory and only reports.

flows.title: Starting up and supervising the model service
flows.summary: npm start brings up Express; Express brings up Python, watches it, and cleans up after it.

steps.title: npm start
steps.text: The prestart hook builds the pages if they are missing, then node app.js runs. Settings come from .env (or TERUCON_ENV_FILE) with the real environment winning.

steps.title: MODEL_SERVICE decides
steps.text: auto (default) starts the Python service as a child process; external uses MODEL_SERVICE_URL and starts nothing; off means no model service at all and the Studio uses its in-browser parser.

steps.title: A usable Python is found
steps.text: An explicit PYTHON is the only candidate. Otherwise: model/.venv, .venv, then python3 and python (Windows: Scripts\python.exe, then py -3). A candidate is accepted only if flask, numpy, PIL, cv2, requests and google.auth import.

steps.title: The child is spawned
steps.text: python -m terucon_model in model/, with MODEL_PORT=0 (the system picks a free port), MODEL_HOST=127.0.0.1, a random per-run MODEL_SERVICE_KEY, MODEL_PARENT_PID, and an explicit environment. Its output lines are prefixed [model].

steps.title: Python binds, then announces
steps.text: It binds the socket first and prints exactly one line, flushed: TERUCON_MODEL_READY http://127.0.0.1:<port>. SAM, if enabled, keeps loading in the background; /health shows loading, then ready.

steps.title: Express goes ready
steps.text: It parses the READY line for the port, checks /health, and the status moves starting, ready. /api/config and /api/health now show model.status = ready.

steps.title: If it dies, it comes back
steps.text: After an unexpected exit it restarts after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 seconds. A sixth exit within ten minutes is not restarted: the service stays unavailable with the reason, and the website keeps serving throughout. A start that only took too long (MODEL_START_TIMEOUT) is reported, not looped.

steps.title: Nothing is left behind
steps.text: Express kills the child on close, SIGINT, SIGTERM and exit. If Express itself is killed hard, the child notices MODEL_PARENT_PID is gone and exits within about 3 seconds.
